hints.content:
We define function $f$ using a definite integral of function $h$. For every $x$-value, we calculate $f(x)$ by taking the definite integral of $h$ from $-1$ to $x$.

So to calculate $f(\goldD{4})$ we need to take the definite integral of $h$ from $-1$ to $\goldD{4}$:

$f(\goldD{4})=\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{\goldD{4}}h(t)\,dt$

This represents the net area between the graph of $h(t)$ and the $x$-axis from $x=-1$ to $x=4$.

We can find $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{\goldD{4}}h(t)\,dt$ using geometric area formulas.

![The graph of function h has the region between the segments and the x-axis, between x = negative 1 and x = 4, shaded. The segment at the top of the shaded region starts at (negative 1, 6), moves upward to (1, 8), moves horizontally to the right and ends at (4, 8).](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/8b9121f5a146274f852cc8593a3e8e1011343f0c)

We have a $5$ by $8$ rectangle less a $2$ by $2$ right triangle, so in total the area is $38$.
